scope: Every paragraph and note on both grammar pages visually reviewed.

source_claims.claim: The source treats Korava as a Tamil dialect, though not derived from present colloquial Tamil, and notes agreements with other Dravidian languages. Retained as historical source interpretation only.
Belgaum, Jamkhandi and Bijapur specimens are described as the same form of speech with slight local variations; named specimens remain separate lect/locality evidence.
Indistinct interchangeable short final vowels; usually dropped final l; optional initial h, compared with Tamil p and Kanarese h. All printed lexical examples retained.
Plural suffixes and origin comparisons, case suffixes and other-language controls retained. Dative/accusative overlap and genitive identity with oblique base retained.
Broad comparison with colloquial Tamil, Kurukh ort, Malayalam raṇḍu and añju, and initial-r phonotactics retained with exact examples.
All paradigm cells retained separately, one first-person plural form, Kanarese/Tamil/Coorgi comparisons retained without assigning all shared grammar to Belgaum.
Present/future/past formation comparisons, all personal endings and eight glossed examples retained. Bare suffixes remain audit-only.
Specimen genre, lect and locality distinctions explicitly retained; table source scope specifically Korvi of Belgaum.

authority_policy: Cited prior works remain bibliographic context; no donor or etymological links inferred from citation alone.
